target_customer: Salaried professionals in the San Francisco Bay Area who can afford a mortgage payment but not a down payment, buying homes priced about US$550K to US$1.75M
problem: Young professionals with steady incomes cannot save a large enough down payment to buy a home in expensive markets.
business_model: Lease-to-own: ZeroDown buys the home with cash, the customer leases it and earns purchase credits; US$10,000 fee per home plus concierge

founders.name: Abhijeet Dwivedi
founders.background_notes: Former chief operating officer at Zenefits per TechCrunch; later chief growth officer at Flyhomes.

founders.name: Laks Srini
founders.background_notes: Former chief technology officer at Zenefits per TechCrunch; later CTO of Flyhomes.

founders.name: Hari Viswanathan
founders.background_notes: Former staff engineer at Zenefits per TechCrunch.

technical_complexity.rationale: Underwriting software and home purchase workflows were standard engineering; the hard parts were structuring a debt-funded real estate fund and operating purchases.

defensibility.rationale: Access to cheap debt capital was the real constraint, and the lease-to-own structure could be copied by better capitalized iBuyers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied the model; Flyhomes bought ZeroDown's assets and team in January 2024, announced June 2024, and used its search technology.

market_need_then: San Francisco housing affordability and rising prices were widely covered; TechCrunch reported the US$30M round in June 2019 on the pitch that stock-grant earners could not meet down payments.

branding.domain_note: Used the exact zerodown.com domain, which now redirects to flyhomes.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission-led copy about the American Dream and housing affordability (YC description).

rebrands.why: Flyhomes acquired ZeroDown and absorbed its technology; the domain redirects to Flyhomes.

brand_strength.rationale: The name states the benefit clearly, and TechCrunch and trade outlets covered the launch, but no evidence of community, merch or brand-driven growth was found.

pivots.to: AI home search technology inside Flyhomes
pivots.why: Flyhomes acquired the assets and team; a financial education site says the consumer rent-to-own program ended, which is unverified.

outcome_analysis: ZeroDown raised US$30M in equity and US$100M in debt in 2019 to buy homes for lease-to-own customers, then was acquired by Flyhomes in January 2024, with 16 staff including two co-founders joining Flyhomes and the product reframed as AI home search. The price was not disclosed. The structure depended on debt capital and a housing market that turned after 2021, but sources found do not state why the business was sold.
notes: The company domain redirects to flyhomes.com. The YC page lists only Dwivedi; the other two founders and their Zenefits roles come from TechCrunch. Founder education was not found. TechCrunch said sources valued the company at over US$70M, which ZeroDown declined to confirm, so no valuation is recorded. The June 2019 round is labeled other because TechCrunch did not call it a Series A; Business Insider reportedly did. The August 2019 debt figure comes from the National Mortgage Professional article and a Business Insider headline in search results. Acquisition date: aggregators say January 2024, announcement was June 2024. Flyhomes then sold its search portal to Real Brokerage in July 2025 per a deal tracker. Competitors such as Divvy Homes (founded 2017) appeared in search results, but no dated source from around mid 2019 was opened, so the list is empty.
